summary: Cecil Bendall (1856–1906) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, Oxford, and under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge as Professor of Sanskrit.

Cecil Y. Lang (1920–2003) studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale (~1949–1951), the University of Chicago (~1967–1970), and the University of Virginia, where he was Professor of English (~1970–1991).

Ch'ing-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a sinologist and japanologist who earned degrees from National Taiwan University and Princeton. He held posts at UC Berkeley, UMass Amherst as Chair of Asian Languages and Literatures, and founded National Dong Hwa University.

Chack-fan Lee (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at The University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972), later serving as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at HKU (1994–2015).
Chaeson Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) and studied under Ekyo Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche (1930–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé.

Chaim Rabin (1915–1996) was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford (Christ Church). He held academic posts at the University of Oxford (1941–1956) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1986).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at Oxford, held research fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford and Clare Hall, Cambridge, taught at National University of Singapore, and was a professor at Lancaster University (attested 2007–2012).

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and other fields. He earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University, where he later served as a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and was a professor at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).

Champa Thupten Zongtse (born 1934) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he is attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer as attested in 2009.
Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Chandrabhāl Tripathi (1929–1996) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen, Cologne, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the Free University of Berlin as Professor of Indology (~1974–1994).
Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. Hwang studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Noritoshi Aramaki and earned a PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as Professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo (1899–1958) was a scholar of linguistics and sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1916–1921), he held posts at Xiamen University, Northwest University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University (~1934–1949).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD attested 2002). Mun's teachers and supervisors included Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, John D. Dunne, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.

Charlene E. Makley is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She serves as associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who studied at Yale (A.B., Ph.D.). He taught at Yale (~1933–1936), served as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1936–1967), and founded and edited Philosophy East and West.

Charles B. Jones is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).
